_meta.anti_fabrication_note: This record represents the Lowe-fixed (NSL) protocol from the same 1996 paper. It is stored as a separate row because it is the SECURE variant — attack_present=0. Source: Lowe 1996 TACAS LNCS 1055 pp.147-166.
_meta.primary_source: Lowe, G. Breaking and Fixing the Needham-Schroeder Public-Key Protocol Using FDR. TACAS 1996, LNCS 1055, pp.147-166. DOI:10.1007/3-540-61042-1_43

paper_title: Breaking and Fixing the Needham-Schroeder Public-Key Protocol Using FDR
equation_source_page: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — confirm page of fixed protocol within pp.147-166
attack_source_page: N/A — this is the secure variant
cryptographic_parameters: Same as NSPK. Fix: B's identity added to Message 2 payload.
original_equations:
A → B : {Na, A}Kb
B → A : {Na, Nb, B}Ka
A → B : {Nb}Kb

normalized_equations.description: Lowe's fix: B's identity B added to the payload. A can now verify the responder's identity before completing.

attacker_identity: N/A — protocol is secure against the Lowe MITM
security_violation: None. Lowe's fix prevents the MITM: when A receives step 2, A sees B's identity inside the decrypted payload. If E tried to relay a step-2 message from a B-session into an A-session with E, A would see B's name (not E's name) and abort.
verified_by: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — confirm fixed equation page against Lowe 1996 PDF
notes: This is the positive/secure example for the NSPK protocol family. Paired with paper_001 (the vulnerable version). Stored separately to provide an attack_present=0 row for dataset balance.
